It is more prone to overfitting in sparse views compared to trilinear interpolation [S3, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and passages that Siddon's method is 'more prone to overfitting in sparse views' compared to trilinear interpolation. Source [S3] corroborates that Siddon's method exactly computes line integrals (intersection lengths) and involves computing intersection parameters (alphas) with parallel planes.
